output: You're right that per-seat pricing rises as more people use the platform, and it's a fair concern when the number of schools keeps changing. For occasional users, we offer lower-cost contributor and viewer seat types, so headteachers who only need to check progress or review reports don't have to be priced like full editors. Multi-year terms can also cap the annual increase. [PLACEHOLDER] pricing example: three-year cost for a company with mostly contributor seats. I'd be glad to model the cost at your expected user count over three years, with the renewal cap options side by side, so you can see how the total changes as new schools join. Could I send that model to you this week?
